title: A Simulation-Free Topological Basis for Building Compact Koopman Models of Protein Folding.
authors: Fakhoury, Ziad; Sosso, Gabriele C; Habershon, Scott
journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
one_liner_zh: 该文提出一种免模拟的图驱动采样（GDS）方法生成蛋白质折叠接触图景观，结合VAMP构建马尔可夫模型以估计折叠时间尺度，属于蛋白质构象采样与动力学建模的计算研究，方法创新且可迁移。
abstract: Unravelling protein-folding mechanisms and kinetics is a key challenge to biochemical science. The variational approach for Markov processes (VAMP) is a powerful tool to build Markov Models that capture key kinetic and structural information despite the conformational complexity and long time scales associated with protein folding. However, VAMP-based Markov models use data from exhaustive molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to construct an underlying basis set describing the "coarse-grained" kinetics; the same MD data can be used to predict transition probabilities between partitioned configuration space, enabling the extraction of folding time scales and mechanism. Here, we propose an alternative strategy for Markov model construction that does not rely on extensive, computationally demanding MD data for configuration space partitioning. Specifically, we show that graph-driven sampling (GDS) can generate a complete "landscape" of intermediate contact-maps linking unfolded and folded protein conformations; importantly, extensive MD simulations are not required in GDS. When combined with a physically intuitive shortest-contact-hop metric to discriminate different intermediate states, GDS mapping of protein-folding configuration space generates a reliable "structurally aware" partitioning for VAMP model construction. To demonstrate this strategy, we show that a GDS-constructed Markov model variationally improves folding time scale estimates for all-atom models of the WW domain protein horizontal line and has the additional advantage of easily resolving kinetic traps in the folding landscape that have proven challenging to confirm otherwise. Together, the combination of GDS and VAMP opens a new route toward rapid characterization of protein-folding intermediates and kinetics traps to help address frontier challenges such as protein misfolding, aggregation, and protein design.
abstract_zh: 解析蛋白质折叠机制和动力学是生物化学科学的一个关键挑战。马尔可夫过程的变分方法（VAMP）是构建马尔可夫模型的强大工具，能够捕捉关键的动力学和结构信息，尽管蛋白质折叠涉及构象复杂性和长时间尺度。然而，基于VAMP的马尔可夫模型利用详尽的分子动力学（MD）模拟数据来构建描述“粗粒度”动力学的基础基组；同一MD数据可用于预测划分构象空间之间的转移概率，从而提取折叠时间尺度和机制。在此，我们提出了一种替代的马尔可夫模型构建策略，该策略不依赖于广泛且计算密集的MD数据进行构象空间划分。具体而言，我们展示了图驱动采样（GDS）能够生成连接未折叠和折叠蛋白质构象的中间接触图谱的完整“景观”；重要的是，GDS中不需要广泛的MD模拟。当与物理直觉的最短接触跳跃度量相结合以区分不同中间状态时，GDS对蛋白质折叠构象空间的映射为VAMP模型构建生成了可靠的“结构感知”划分。为演示此策略，我们展示了GDS构建的马尔可夫模型在变分上改善了WW结构域蛋白水平线的全原子模型的折叠时间尺度估计，并具有轻松解析折叠景观中动力学陷阱的额外优势，而这些陷阱在其他方法中难以确认。总之，GDS与VAMP的结合开辟了一条快速表征蛋白质折叠中间体和动力学陷阱的新途径，有助于应对蛋白质错误折叠、聚集和蛋白质设计等前沿挑战。
